pdf-to-html.metaDescription: Convert PDF to HTML online for free. Extracts text in reading order into clean semantic HTML with page sections. Download instantly. Private — runs in your browser.
pdf-to-html.keywords: pdf to html, convert pdf to html, pdf to html online, extract pdf text to html
pdf-to-html.quickAnswer: Upload a PDF and its text is extracted in reading order into a clean, self-contained HTML file — paragraphs, page sections, and proper document structure with built-in styling — ready to open in any browser or paste into a website.
keyFacts: Text is grouped into lines by vertical position, then into paragraphs by spacing.
Each PDF page becomes its own <section> with a page heading.
The output is a single self-contained .html file with inline CSS — no dependencies.
Live stats show pages, words, and characters before you download.
Direction-aware: Arabic PDFs get dir='rtl' automatically.
howTo: Click extract and watch the per-page progress bar.
Review the stats and the text preview in the code window.
Download the .html file and open it in any browser.
pdf-to-html.workedExample: A 5-page product manual: extraction yields 5 <section> blocks, ~2,300 words, 14,800 characters. The downloaded HTML opens in any browser as a readable document you can restyle with your own CSS or paste into a CMS — no PDF reader needed.
benefits: Semantic HTML — real paragraphs and sections, not absolutely-positioned divs.
Self-contained file with inline styles works anywhere, offline.
Reading-order heuristic handles multi-column text sensibly.
RTL detection keeps Arabic documents correctly oriented.
Zero upload — sensitive documents never leave your device.
limitations: Text only — images, charts, and complex tables are not carried over.
Exact visual layout is not preserved; this is about readable content, not pixel fidelity.
Scanned PDFs have no text to extract — OCR is not included.
Unusual fonts or encodings can produce garbled characters.
pdf-to-html.privacyNote: Text extraction runs entirely in your browser with pdf.js. Your document is never uploaded or stored.

faqs.q: Is this the same as PDF to Text?
faqs.a: Similar extraction, different output: PDF to Text gives plain text, while this produces structured HTML with paragraphs, page sections, and styling — ready for the web.

faqs.q: Will the HTML look like my PDF?
faqs.a: No — and that is intentional. You get clean, readable, semantic content you can restyle, not a pixel-perfect replica. For visual fidelity, convert pages to images instead.
Tables come through as plain text lines (structure is lost), and images are skipped. Complex layouts need manual cleanup after conversion.

faqs.q: Why is my scanned PDF empty?
faqs.a: Scans are pictures of text with no embedded characters. This tool extracts embedded text only; scanned documents need OCR software first.

faqs.q: Can I edit the HTML afterwards?
faqs.a: Absolutely — it's standard HTML with inline CSS. Open it in any editor, change the styles, or paste sections into your website.

faqs.q: Does it handle Arabic or Hindi text?
faqs.a: Yes. Extracted Unicode text is preserved, and Arabic documents automatically get right-to-left direction in the output.
